Plan: Tomate in the status bar

A small widget beside your clock that shows the running timer. You can see how much focus time is left from any workspace, and start or pause with one click without opening the window.

~/Work/tomate/docs/bar-widget-plan.html · tomate · 2026-11-14
1 · Background2 · Intuition3 · The widget4 · Optional panel5 · Choose6 · Build7 · Quiz

1Background

How the Omarchy bar works, and why Tomate can plug into it easily.

Beginner ramp (skip if you like)
  • The bar at the top of your screen is the Omarchy shell, one long-running program (built on Quickshell) that draws the bar, notifications and panels.
  • Each item on the bar (clock, weather, Wi-Fi…) is a plugin. You can add your own in ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/. Your Superwhisper panel is one.
  • Which plugins appear where is set in ~/.config/omarchy/shell.json, and the bar reloads as soon as that file is saved.

Tomate already has the hard part: tomate status --json reports what the timer is doing in about 15 milliseconds. The widget only needs to call it once a second and draw the answer. Because the bar and the window read the same database, they can never disagree. If you pause from the bar, the window shows paused too.

tomate.db→ tomate status --json→ bar widget→ click → tomate toggle

A bonus you get for free

Today a block only ends (and notifies you) while something is checking the timer. With the widget always running, notifications arrive on time even when the Tomate window is closed.

Placement: right after the clock (the bar’s centerEnd section), before the world clocks and weather. You can move it later with omarchy bar move.

The five states

Something is running

Focusingaccent ring + countdown + project
The mini ring empties as the block runs, like the big one in the app. The project name is shortened to fit the bar.
On a breakgreen ☕ + countdown
No project name, because you’re not working on anything. Long breaks use your theme’s purple.

Needs you / quiet

Pauseddimmed ⏸ with time left
Dimmed so it doesn’t catch your eye, but the time left stays visible.
Waiting for youamber ▶, flashes 3 times
When a break ends and auto-start is off, the widget flashes briefly so you notice even if you missed the notification. One click starts the next block.
Idlea single small ◔
Takes almost no space. The tooltip still shows today’s total.

Mouse

Left-clickstart / pause / resume
Right-clickopen the Tomate window
Scrollnothing, so you can’t change anything by accident

4Optional: a dropdown panel

With this extra, a left-click opens a small panel like Omarchy’s own Wi-Fi or audio panels, instead of pausing straight away. You could run your whole day from it.

Clicking a project in the list switches the timer to it. If a block is running, the block moves to that project too.

5Choose

Both use the same widget on the bar. The only difference is what a left-click does.

A · Compact widget

  • Left-click pauses or resumes instantly
  • Right-click opens the app for everything else
  • Quick to build: about one sitting
Recommended to start

B · Widget + panel

  • Left-click opens the panel (one extra click to pause)
  • Switch project, skip and stop without the window
  • About twice the work; it can be added on top of A later
Either way

The widget lives in your own plugins folder (~/.config/omarchy/plugins/tomate.bar), so Omarchy updates won’t overwrite it. Removing it is one line in shell.json.

6Build

Three short steps for option A. Option B would add a fourth.

Plugin next

A widget that appears on the bar and reads the timer.

Create the plugin folder
Modelled on Omarchy’s own bar widgets, with a manifest and one QML file, in ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/tomate.bar/.
Poll tomate status --json every second
Show nothing if Tomate isn’t installed or the command fails, so the bar never breaks.
Done when: the countdown on the bar matches the app

States + clicks later

The five states, the tooltip and the mouse actions.

Draw the mini ring and colours from the theme
Accent for focus, green for breaks, purple for long breaks, dimmed when paused, amber flash when ready.
Wire the clicks
Left: tomate toggle. Right: open the Tomate window.
Treat text as plain text
Project names and notes are your own text. They are drawn as plain text, never as markup, following Omarchy’s plugin safety rules.
Done when: every state looks right and clicks work

Place + check later

On your bar, right after the clock.

Add it to shell.json
Insert it at the start of centerEnd, after making a backup of the file. The bar reloads on save.
Check it on your real screen
Screenshot the bar in your current theme and switch themes once to check the colours follow.
Done when: you see ◔ next to your clock

Panel only for B

The dropdown from section 4.

Build it on Omarchy’s panel component
Using the shell’s own panel component, so it opens and animates like the Wi-Fi and audio panels.
Buttons and project list
Each button runs a tomate command; the project list comes from a new tomate projects --json.
Done when: a full focus cycle can be run from the panel alone

7Quiz

Five quick checks.

1. You pause from the bar. What does the open Tomate window show?

✅ B. Both the bar and the window read the same database. The window re-reads it twice a second, so it shows the pause almost immediately.

2. What does a right-click on the widget do?

✅ C. Only harmless actions are on the bar: left-click toggles, right-click opens the app. Stop and skip stay in the app (or the panel, in option B) so a stray click can’t end a block.

3. Why does the widget flash amber three times?

✅ A. When auto-start is off, the timer stops at “ready” and waits. The short flash catches your eye in case you missed the notification; one click starts the block.

4. What changes for notifications once the widget is on the bar?

✅ B. Whichever process notices a phase ending first sends the notification, inside a database lock, so it happens once. The bar checks every second, so that is always on time.

5. What is the difference between option A and option B?

✅ C. The widget on the bar is identical. B adds a panel on left-click, and it can be built on top of A at any time.
